iPhone 18 Pro is just weeks away from launch, and given the major overhaul of this year's lineup, it will become Apple's new standard model like never before.

This year there's no base iPhone 18, and the iPhone 18 Pro will become Apple's new standard model

For years, Apple has released multiple new iPhones every year, and that will undoubtedly continue for many years to come.

However, this fall's iPhone lineup is reportedly set for a major reshuffle.

Apple will no longer offer the usual choice of a standard 'iPhone' and an 'iPhone Pro', and the base iPhone 18 will be completely absent.

Multiple reports indicate that Apple has delayed the launch of the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 until early 2027, leaving only the following devices in this fall's lineup:

By pushing the iPhone 18 out beyond the typical release cycle, the iPhone 18 Pro has essentially become Apple's new standard model for this fall.

Users looking for a more affordable option can still choose last year's iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, or iPhone Air. However, throughout the fall and the entire holiday shopping season, in all of Apple's and partner carrier marketing, the 'iPhone 18' will not be promoted as the new standard model; the iPhone 18 Pro will fill that gap.

The iPhone Ultra's pricing is likely too high to appeal to a broad audience.

So for the average consumer who just wants a 'new iPhone', Apple is essentially offering only two choices: the 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max.

This is an interesting gamble that could make the iPhone 18 Pro the best-selling Pro model of its generation. But combined with expected price increases, there's also risk for Apple. Potential upgraders, with no iPhone 18 to upgrade to, may simply hold onto their current iPhones for longer.

Regardless, in a few months we'll find out if Apple's new strategy works.

What do you think of Apple's changes to the iPhone lineup this year? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
